transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Renee (Redwood SE), Lina (Mirage Head of Security), Tom (Mirage CTO), Ishaan (Platform)

Optional summary (auto):
- Initial security/governance scoping for potential Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment.
- Primary concerns: audit logs retention, SSO/SAML integration, BYOK/KMS key rotation, SOC2/ISO evidence, data residency and retention policy.
- Agreed next steps: exchange SOC2 and ISO artifacts, schedule tech deep dive, pilot scope + pricing.

Transcript body:
00:00 Avery (AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro — i'm avery, i'm the account exec on this. samir and renee from our solutions eng team will cover the technical side. lina, tom, ishaan, thanks for joining. how's the audio for folks?
00:12 Lina: good here, can hear you. i'm lina, head of security at mirage. we wanted to run through your hosting options and specifically how redwood handles keys, logs and ss o — s s o, sorry, s s o and saml.
00:23 Tom: and i'm tom - CTO. main trigger is we need an inference layer for customer-facing features but must stay within our compliance guardrails.
00:31 Samir (SE): great. quick agenda: 1) high level hosting options and differences; 2) auth and iam (sso, saml, scim, rbac); 3) encryption and kms; 4) audit logs and retention; 5) questions and pilot planning.
00:45 Ishaan: timeline wise, we're hoping to decide by end of q1, pilot in late feb if feasible.
00:52 Avery: perfect. lina, from a security standpoint, what are your must-haves?
01:00 Lina: must-haves: SOC2 Type II evidence, ISO 27001 is preferred, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC with fine-grained roles, all request/response audit logs retained for at least 1 year (audit grade), keys managed by our KMS or BYOK, and proof of encryption at rest and in transit. also we need region-specific data residency for EU and US customers.
01:22 Renee: ok noted. on SOC2 we have the latest Type II report and can share a redacted copy. ISO 27001 — we don't hold certificate ourselves for hosted, but we have an iso-aligned control set and customer guidance. is iso a hard requirement or a nice-to-have?
01:38 Lina: it's preferred but SOC2 is required. if you can map your controls to iso that'll help the audit team.
01:45 Samir: we'll include a control mapping doc. on SSO, we support SAML 2.0 and SAML metadata exchange; we also support SCIM for provisioning. customers can configure SAML IdP in the console or for private deployments, we can deploy the control plane in your VPC and hook into your IdP directly.
02:02 Ishaan: for SCIM, do you support group sync and custom attributes? our provisioning uses groups to gate models and endpoints.
02:09 Samir: yes, group sync is supported. custom attributes are ok but need mapping; we'll share attribute mapping templates.
02:17 Tom: and RBAC — can we create per-team and per-model roles? we want devs to be able to deploy but not access customer PII or logs.
02:26 Renee: we have role templates and support custom roles. for Hosted, RBAC is enforced in the console and API with audit trails. for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IAM and sync roles via SCIM + SAML.
02:38 Lina: what about audit logs — where are they stored, how long, and can we ship to our SIEM?
02:45 Samir: we store request metadata and admin actions; payloads optionally can be logged or redacted. default retention in Hosted is 90 days, but for Enterprise customers we can extend retention or push logs to your S3/CloudWatch/Datadog via log forwarding. for Dedicated/Private deployments, logs live in your VPC and are fully in your control.
03:05 Lina: 90 days isn't acceptable — we need 12 months for the app audit. can you confirm push-to-SIEM and encryption in transit?
03:13 Samir: yes, push-to-SIEM supported — we use TLS for transport, logs can be encrypted at rest with KMS. for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) via integrations with major cloud KMS — but important note, with Hosted we manage the runtime; keys can be stored in your KMS and used for envelope encryption.
03:33 Lina: dig into that: are keys ever in Redwood control plane or do you perform any plaintext decryption?
03:39 Renee: we use envelope encryption. root keys stay in your KMS (you rotate them). Redwood holds ephemeral keys for the runtime when necessary but cannot export your root key. for Private deployments, customer controls all keys and runtimes.
03:53 Ishaan: any HSM options? we need FIPS-140 requirement for certain customers.
04:00 Samir: we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS like AWS CloudHSM or GCP KMS with HSM protection; that meets FIPS requirements in most regions.
04:10 Tom: GDPR and data residency — we have EU users, so we need control over which region inference happens in and whether any customer content leaves region. how does Redwood route requests?
04:20 Samir: routing policy can pin a region per-tenant; Hosted supports regional endpoints (we have eu-west, us-central etc). we also have options to deploy a private control plane in your VPC for strict residency. note: some model variants may require different hardware that isn't in every region; we'll fall back only to regionally approved variants per your policy.
04:45 Lina: retention policy: we need both logs and model interaction data to be deletable on request and a retention hold for legal reasons. does your platform support on-demand purge?
04:55 Renee: yes, we support deletion APIs and retention policies. for Hosted, we have a documented delete workflow and can run a purge, but customers should schedule deletes and we provide attestations. for Dedicated/Private, deletion is under your control.
05:10 Ishaan: latency/cost tradeoffs matter — if we route to eu region and pinned to smaller model, can you support autoscaling?
05:18 Samir: Dedicated supports configurable pools and autoscaling policies; Hosted has auto burst but capacity not guaranteed like Dedicated. for strict SLOs, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
05:30 Tom: from procurement side, what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated?
05:34 Avery: usually a 3-month reserved capacity pilot or a 12-month contract for commit pricing. we'll send specifics.
05:40 Lina: auditors will ask for evidence: SOC2 attestation, encryption architecture diagram, key rotation logs, and RBAC matrix. can you provide sample artifacts?
05:51 Avery: yes, we'll share SOC2, architecture diagram, and an RBAC example mapping.
05:56 Samir: also we can provide a short demo of audit log delivery into your SIEM during the deep dive.
06:02 Lina: one more — session-level PII scrubbing. can you redact sensitive fields from prompts before persisting?
06:10 Renee: we support both client-side scrubbing patterns and server-side redaction hooks; we can drop payload recording entirely or run a transformation pipeline that masks PII using regex or ML-based scrubbers. caveat: masking may affect evals.
06:25 Ishaan: about SSO failover — if your hosted auth path has outage, do you support fallback?
06:30 Samir: yes, we recommend having a cached service account token for emergency failover and we have a multi-idp setup for high availability. for Dedicated/Private this is in-customer control.
06:42 Tom: okay. can you describe the control plane separation for Private? does Redwood push updates or do we manage it?
06:48 Samir: for Private, we offer two modes: 1) Customer-managed control plane — we provide images and helm charts, you run and manage; 2) Managed Private — we operate the control plane inside your VPC with customer network isolation but Redwood has limited admin access under a contractual ops window. both have options for patching cadence.
07:10 Lina: how are emergency patches handled? we need an SLA for critical vulnerabilities.
07:16 Renee: for Dedicated/Private we have an agreed patch window and emergency patch process; for Hosted we issue critical patches and inform customers, with scheduled maintenance windows. we can include a security bulletin and notify your security channels.
07:28 Ishaan: question on logging verbosity — do you capture full request/response bodies by default?
07:33 Samir: by default we capture metadata and truncated bodies; full dumps are opt-in and flagged as high-sensitivity logs. we can tailor retention and redaction.
07:43 Lina: does redwood support log integrity checks or append-only audit stores?
07:48 Samir: yes, we support immutable append-only logs via object lock on S3 for Dedicated/Private and can include checksums. for Hosted we can provide tamper-evident logs and notarization if required.
08:02 Tom: what's typical lead time to stand up a Dedicated pool with our VPC peering and BYOK?
08:09 Avery: usually 4-6 weeks for Dedicated with a standard onboarding, faster for a pilot using pre-approved configs. Private with full deployment is more like 8-12 weeks depending on network approvals.
08:21 Ishaan: SAML metadata — any quirks we need to know? our IdP requires signed assertions and encrypted nameid.
08:27 Samir: we support signed assertions and encrypted assertions. we also support signed logout and name id formats. we'll give you the attribute mapping doc.
08:36 Lina: audit question: can you provide history of key rotations? auditors want proof of rotation and who triggered it.
08:42 Renee: yes, key rotation events are logged. for Hosted BYOK we show rotation timestamps and KMS ARNs; for Private it's under your KMS logs.
08:51 Tom: encryption at rest — are model weights encrypted?
08:55 Samir: weights are encrypted at rest in storage and in transit between nodes. runtime caches use ephemeral keys. for Dedicated/Private we can guarantee keys are customer controlled.
09:08 Lina: do you have penetration test reports or a third-party pen test?
09:12 Avery: we run regular pen tests and can share executive summaries and scopes; full reports can be shared under NDA.
09:20 Ishaan: is there an audit trail linking API keys, tokens, and user identities? we need to map actions back to personas.
09:27 Samir: yes, we correlate token usage with user identities via our auth layer. for SAML users we map assertions to user ids.
09:33 Tom: what about token rotation and short-lived tokens?
09:37 Renee: API keys can be short-lived; we support automatic rotation via our SDK and ephemeral tokens tied to the IdP.
09:45 Lina: ok — for pilot scope, we'll need a set of acceptance criteria: no logs > 12 months, successful SAML integration in test tenant, BYOK demonstration, and audit log delivery to our SIEM.
09:59 Avery: we can align on that. i'll draft an acceptance checklist and share in the next 48 hours.
10:06 Samir: suggested pilot: 3 nodes dedicated pool, eu-west + us, test dataset with synthetic PII and end-to-end log forwarding. run for 2 weeks.
10:18 Ishaan: cost estimate for that?
10:21 Avery: i'll include a pilot pricing sheet — usually discounted pilot rate for a 2-week window.
10:26 Tom: legal will want data processing addendum and standard contract clauses; ave ry, can legal send us the DPA?
10:33 Avery: yes, i'll circle legal and attach a DPA.
10:37 Lina: last question — do you have a SOC2 bridge letter for the last quarter? sometimes our auditors ask for that while waiting for a new report.
10:45 Avery: we do provide bridge letters on request; i'll include that pack.
10:49 Ishaan: any gotchas with model quantization and private deployments? sometimes quantized kernels rely on signed binaries.
10:57 Samir: good note — certain quantized kernels have hardware constraints; we'll share the model compatibility matrix. for Private we ship the compatible runtime and validated kernels.
11:08 Tom: cool. let's recap quick next steps.
11:12 Avery: recap: 1) send SOC2 + ISO mapping + pen test exec summary + DPA (Avery) 2) Samir to schedule deep technical demo and audit log demo with SIEM integration; 3) Lina to send SAML metadata and retention policy; 4) agree pilot scope and pricing.
11:29 Lina: that sounds right. thanks everyone.
11:32 Avery: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
11:35 (call ends)
